subject: Mythology
title: Inari: God of Rice and Foxes
description: Learn Inari: God of Rice and Foxes in one minute.

hook.text: Inari is the most popular kami in Japan, with over 30,000 shrines — more than any other deity.

buildup.text: Originally the god of rice and harvests, Inari's role expanded to include business, industry, and general prosperity.

discovery.text: Foxes serve as Inari's divine messengers. That's why fox statues guard the entrance to every Inari shrine.

twist.text: Inari has no fixed gender. The deity appears as male, female, or androgynous depending on the shrine and tradition.

climax.text: Fushimi Inari in Kyoto, with its thousands of red torii gates, is one of the most visited places in all of Japan.

punchline.text: The most worshipped god in Japan has no fixed face — only fox messengers.

quiz.question: Why are fox statues found at Inari shrines?
options: Foxes are believed to be Inari's divine messengers
Inari was originally a fox who became a god
Foxes guard the rice fields from evil spirits
